text:
maria: Heads-up — we started getting p95/p99 latency complaints from a customer after yesterday's runtime rollout to eu-west-1 (canary -> 30%). Seeing tails jump mostly on generation endpoints. Investigating now.

aj: Which runtime version was rolled?

maria: runtime v2.14.0 with the new kernel-selector heuristics and an updated batching default (max_batch 64 -> 128). Canary at 30% since 04:15 UTC.

yvette: Noted similar alerts from synth traffic. p50 fine, p95 up ~60ms, p99 up ~300ms on long prompts (>1024 tokens).

metrics-bot: Auto-alert — p99_gen_latency_eu_west1 increased from 220ms -> 520ms at 04:22 UTC (rolling 5m).

maria: I ran a quick PromQL to isolate: `sum(rate(gen_latency_bucket{region="eu-west-1",le!="+Inf"}[5m])) by (le)` — shows heavier mass in higher buckets after 04:15.

kevin: Can you dump the canary routing? maybe traffic is hitting a fallback path or cold-starts?

maria: Route table looks normal. Canary nodes appear to have higher queue times. Getting stack traces from one canary pod: 
```
[2026-03-10T04:18:12.345Z] request_id=abc123 queue_wait=78ms kernel_select=heuristic_v3 kv_cache_hit=false batch_size=96
[2026-03-10T04:18:12.346Z] model_infer_start=2026-03-10T04:18:12.346Z model_infer_time=180ms
```

aj: Batch 96 — that’s big. Could be model memory thrashing / CUDA scheduling causing tail latency. Did batching change per-tenant limits?

maria: Batching changed globally to allow up to 128 to improve throughput; we didn't restrict on canary.

yvette: Suggestion: reduce max_batch for canary to 64 and re-run. Also toggle kernel-selector back to v2 for canary nodes to see if it helps.

oncall-bot: @oncall paged. Severity: high for impacted customer latency.

maria: Trying quick mitigation: patching canary runtime config — set `max_batch=64` and `kernel_selector=heuristic_v2` for the canary nodepool. Applying now.

deploy-bot: Rolling update initiated on nodepool canary-eu-west1 (3 nodes).

kevin: While that's rolling, can we bisect which change is responsible? Two changes in v2.14.0: batching default and kernel selector heuristics. We should promote only one revert at a time.

am: (typo) aj: Agreed. We can temporarily set batching to old value and keep kernel change; then if that fixes, batching is culprit. If not, flip kernel.

maria: Patch applied. Observing metrics...

metrics-bot: p99_gen_latency_eu_west1: 520ms -> 330ms after nodepool patch (5m window). p95 fell back near baseline.

maria: Nice. Early signal that larger batches were amplifying tail.

yvette: Can we reproduce with synthetic load locally? run a long-prompt workload with batch saturation to confirm. Use `ab_test.sh` with concurrency=64 and payload length ~1500 tokens.

aj: Repro run logs: 
```
./ab_test.sh --concurrency 64 --payload-tokens 1500 --target runtime-canary:443
observed p99 480ms with max_batch=128
observed p99 210ms with max_batch=64
```

kevin: OK that’s pretty conclusive. Batching default increase is causing higher p99 for long sequences. Throughput wins for short prompts maybe, but tails worse for long.

maria: For now, we'll keep canary at max_batch=64 and roll this config change out to dedicated nodes where customers reported latency degradation. Also add per-route max_batch overrides so large-sequence routes don't get saturated.

yvette: Also want a longer-term fix: make kernel-selector aware of sequence length and estimated GPU memory for the batch, or add adaptive batch sizing that caps effective batch for long sequences. Filed a ticket in sprint board.

aj: Can we add a safeguard: when p99 > threshold for a route after a rollout, automatically revert batching to previous value for that canary group?

maria: We can do an automated canary policy: if p99_gen_latency increases >40% and error budget impact > X, rollback config changes for the canary. I'll draft the policy.

metrics-bot: Saved dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/xyz/canary-bisect-1923456789

oncall-bot: Incident updated: initial mitigation applied, customer notified.

kevin: Notes for postmortem: 1) Two simultaneous optimizations (batching + kernel selector) made bisect harder. 2) No per-route batch caps. 3) Canary group allowed full global defaults — should be limited. 4) Need regression tests with long-prompt synthetic workloads in CI.

maria: I'll compile a short incident summary and rollout checklist. For immediate follow-ups: roll config to dedicated nodes, add per-route override, add automated canary rollback policy, create e2e synthetic test, and queue kernel-selector enhancements.

yvette: Thanks all. Customer reported improved latency after mitigation. Closing loop once we finish the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Great job triaging quickly.

maria: Filing final notes in the incident tracker and will attach perf traces and the ab_test logs.

metrics-bot: Collected artifacts: trace IDs [tr-0a1b2c, tr-0d3e4f], ab_test logs uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1923456789/

maria: End of thread — will update when postmortem is live.
